clue.text: French master responsible for courses

parts.note: the French word for a chief or master is also our word for the cook in charge of a meal's courses, so 'courses' can mislead towards teaching or racing

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster from France who organises the lesson courses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master' and 'courses' suggest a teacher planning lessons; in the kitchen the courses are parts of a meal, and the French word for the boss is the word we use for the head cook.
explanation.definitionFit: A head cook runs a kitchen and sends out each course of a meal; the title comes from the French for chief.

clue.text: Bearing the cost of transport

definitions.meaning: one's bearing is one's posture or deportment
the charge made for conveying goods

explanation.surface: Someone shouldering the expense of shipping something.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both deportment, how a person holds themselves, and the fee charged for conveying goods.

clue.text: Learner — one from a part of Austria?

definitions.text: one from a part of Austria?
definitions.meaning: playfully, a person from the Tyrol, an Austrian region, as if the region's name gave its native this word; the question mark flags the whimsy

explanation.surface: Asking whether a beginner hails from some region of Austria.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a joke rather than a dictionary sense: the Tyrol is an Alpine region of Austria, and dropping its final L makes a mock name for one of its people.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice or beginner in any field is called by this word, borrowed from Latin for a recruit.

clue.text: He appreciates the exquisite tea these provide

indicators.note: the letters of the words tea these are made to provide, by rearrangement, a different word

explanation.surface: A connoisseur appreciates the fine tea these places serve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provide' signals that TEA THESE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with refined sensibility to beauty and art is one who appreciates the exquisite.

clue.text: Drink, when cold, can go the wrong way

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: going the wrong way means the words can go are read backwards

explanation.surface: A drink in a cold can might be swallowed the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' turns CAN GO round to OGNAC, which follows C.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a brandy from the Charente region of France, a classic after-dinner spirit.

clue.text: Records the development of Wessex town

indicators.note: development means the letters of records the are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Archives chart how a town in south-west England grew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development of' signals rearranging RECORDS THE. Wessex is Thomas Hardy's name for south-west England; this Dorset county town is his Casterbridge.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the county town of Dorset, in the region Hardy's novels call Wessex.

clue.text: Prince demolished part of a king crab

indicators.note: something demolished is knocked down and its parts rearranged, so the word prince is reworked

explanation.surface: A royal destroying a piece of shellfish at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demolished' signals rearranging PRINCE; 'king' plays on the royal but belongs to the crab.
explanation.definitionFit: A crab's claw, the jointed pincher at the end of a limb, is called by this name.

clue.text: Part of the Burma-Siam landmass

indicators.note: the letters needed form part of the run Burma-Siam, sitting across the hyphen

explanation.surface: A region comprising Burma and Siam, now Myanmar and Thailand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' signals letters hidden inside BURMA-SIAM.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the largest continent, the great landmass of which Burma and Siam are part.

clue.text: Overweight actor playing the villain?

definitions.meaning: in theatre and film slang the bad guy role, and its player, is so called

explanation.surface: A portly performer cast as the bad guy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both fat and, in show-business slang, the villain of a piece or the actor in that part.

clue.text: Coins come into this field of study

indicators.note: the words coins come are turned into something else, a rearranged word

explanation.surface: Money is central to a certain academic discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' signals that COINS COME is rearranged; the surface is nearly &lit, since coins really do come into the subject.
explanation.definitionFit: The academic discipline concerned with money, production and trade is a field of study.

clue.text: Do without lost tent that's been left behind

parts.note: to forgo something is to do without it

indicators.note: lost suggests the word tent is in disarray, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A camper managing without a mislaid tent left at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do without' looks like the definition but supplies the first piece; 'lost' is the anagram signal for tent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left behind and not remembered has slipped from the mind, the participle of failing to recall.

clue.text: Come out with me more than once to have a drink

indicators.note: more than once means the remaining letters appear twice
out with means the word me is thrown out of the word come

explanation.surface: An invitation to come out repeatedly with someone for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out with' is read as 'out with me!', ejecting that word; 'more than once' doubles what is left before the A.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a hot chocolate beverage, made from powdered cacao beans.

clue.text: One or two items on the afternoon menu?

definitions.text: One or two items on the afternoon menu?

parts.words: One or two items on the afternoon menu?
parts.note: the answer is one bun, but split into its two halves it names two separate things served at an afternoon break

explanation.surface: A few dishes offered at afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One or two' reads as 'a few', but means the item is one thing that is also two: the drink and the sweet baked treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, sweet, toasted bun with dried fruit is a classic British afternoon tea item.

clue.text: She has the advantage, when climbing

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the letters run upwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an asset is an advantage or useful quality

explanation.surface: A woman holds the upper hand as she ascends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when climbing' turns ASSET upwards; 'She' is a woman's name as definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, so 'she' stands for a particular female person.

clue.text: There's a lack of variety, still

explanation.surface: Things are monotonous, as they still are.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both identical, with nothing varied, and nonetheless, as a sentence adverb.

clue.text: Brightened up, when found not guilty

definitions.meaning: said of weather or a sky that has become fine

explanation.surface: A defendant's mood lifts on being acquitted.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes both skies turning fine and a defendant acquitted of a charge.

clue.text: Suit oneself

parts.note: the idiom means please yourself, but read literally it is putting a suit on one's own body, clothing oneself

explanation.surface: A shrug: do as you please.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'suit oneself' means do what you like; read literally it means clothe yourself in a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: To put clothes on oneself is, literally, to suit oneself.

clue.text: Splendid organ effect

definitions.meaning: a pipe organ's ... box opens shutters to make the sound louder

explanation.surface: Praise for a fine sound from a church organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is old slang for excellent and the name of an organ's crescendo mechanism, also a rising volume.

clue.text: Little fellow not depressed, just confused

definitions.text: Little fellow not depressed, just confused

indicators.note: confused means the remaining letters are jumbled
not means the word for depressed is taken away from the word fellow

parts.note: low means depressed or down in spirits

explanation.surface: A small chap who is not glum, merely bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes LOW from FELLOW, leaving FEL; 'confused' rearranges it. The whole clue also pictures a mischievous little sprite.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mischievous sprite of folklore is a little fellow, and often a puzzled-looking one.

clue.text: Expect warning shout to players

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shout warning of an incoming ball
the cast is the set of actors in a production

explanation.surface: Anticipating a cry of alarm to performers.
explanation.definitionFit: To predict something is to expect it ahead of time, as with the weather.

clue.text: After time, ceremony becomes commonplace

indicators.note: after means the ceremony word follows the time letter

explanation.surface: A ritual repeated over time grows stale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places RITE after T.
explanation.definitionFit: Hackneyed, overused and unoriginal, so ordinary or commonplace.

clue.text: Disenchanted, dash out upset, it's lewd.

indicators.note: out means the letters of dash are taken out of the word disenchanted, scattered though they are
upset means the letters remaining are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone disillusioned rushes out, troubled by something obscene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes D, A, S, H from DISENCHANTED, leaving IENCNTED; 'upset' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewd behaviour offends against decency, so it is improper or obscene.

clue.text: One more metamorphosis on earth

indicators.note: a metamorphosis is a change of form, so the words on earth take a new shape

explanation.surface: Yet another transformation in the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'metamorphosis' rearranges ON EARTH.
explanation.definitionFit: An additional one, a further example of the same kind, is one more.

clue.text: Choose one mother — the best!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Pick one mother, she's the finest of all!
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of the Latin-derived word for the most favourable result, the best ones.

clue.text: Mounting a revolt

explanation.surface: Launching an insurrection.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both ascending or climbing and an uprising against authority.

clue.text: Red rose embroidered for church screen

indicators.note: embroidered suggests the words red rose are worked into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A rose stitched in red on a church's decorated screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embroidered' rearranges RED ROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental screen or panel behind a church altar.

clue.text: Fruit goes out of fashion

definitions.meaning: the sweet fruit of a palm

explanation.surface: Some fruit falls from favour.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names palm fruits and also means becomes outmoded, as style that ages badly.

clue.text: Rather dull sailor put under the doctor

indicators.note: in a down clue put under means the sailor letters go below the doctor letters

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A boring seaman placed in a medic's care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put under' places AB below DR in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreary, colourless and lacking interest, so fairly dull.

clue.text: Scared, possibly by bully — one given undue respect

indicators.note: possibly means the word scared could be rearranged into another word

parts.note: to cow is to bully or intimidate

explanation.surface: Someone frightened by an intimidator who is held in awe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges SCARED.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for an institution or idea beyond criticism, after the cattle revered in Hinduism.

clue.text: Yes, about to include parking spot

indicators.note: to include means the parking letter is placed inside
about means the word yes is turned around into a new order

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Agreeing to include a space for parking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges YES to ESY, and 'to include' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch sight of something is to spot it.

clue.text: A pack animal?

parts.note: a pack animal usually means a beast of burden, but here it is a predator that hunts in a pack

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack animal' suggests a mule or donkey carrying loads; the question mark points to a creature that lives in a pack.
explanation.definitionFit: This wild canine hunts in packs, so it is literally an animal of the pack.

clue.text: Munitions produced by man and master

indicators.note: produced by means the letters of man and master are worked into something new

explanation.surface: Weapons manufactured by a worker and his boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced by' rearranges MAN and MASTER together.
explanation.definitionFit: Weapons and military equipment are both munitions, collectively.

clue.text: Penal reform board

indicators.note: reform means the word penal is formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A committee charged with prison reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges PENAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A committee or body of people appointed to decide matters is a board.
